note: The angles the game asks for. Archetypes and paint bands are NOT repeated
here — they are read from models.json, which stays the one place a model
mapping or a paint band lives. Two copies of that table is exactly the
corpse CLAUDE.md warns about: nothing fails when they disagree, the frames
just quietly render the wrong car.
tiltDegrees is measured off STRAIGHT DOWN, matching the Blender script and
SPRITE_TILT_DEGREES in camera.ts: 0 is a floor plan, 90 is a side
elevation. yawDegrees swings the camera right, the same direction the lot
camera's yaw goes.
The lot. Sixty of these share a screen at 34-60px, which is where the
shading earns its keep.
12 degrees, and NOT the lot camera's 25, because LotScene lays a top-down
frame on the ground through its own rotate-and-squash: the render's own
foreshortening composes with that one, so shooting at 25 would
double-count it and squash the car by 15% instead of 9%. Baking the full
25/25 projection means the scene stops transforming the art at all, which
is a different change to a different file. SPRITE_TILT_DEGREES is the
honest record of where these came from and must match this number.
aspect is the CAR_BOX artboard from src/ui/lot/layout.ts, pinned so the
lot positions these frames exactly as it always has.
The feed and the sheets, where one car fills the card at 96px and 220px.
Ships at 512 because 220 logical points is 660 physical on a phone, and at
288 the card was visibly soft. The palette step in render.js is what makes
that affordable: these are a third the size of the 288px frames were.
A three-quarter shot rather than a flat elevation, because this is the
'listing photograph' angle the vector renderer was always approximating
and could not reach: an elevation shows one flank and no roof, which is
the least flattering way to photograph a car and the reason forecourt
photos are never taken that way.
62 degrees off vertical is 28 above the ground — high enough to show the
roof and the bonnet, low enough that the car still reads as standing on
something. Yawed 34 so the near front wing leads.
No aspect: the box is fitted to the geometry, because nothing downstream
depends on this artboard's shape. CarArt takes the height from the frame.
